name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags any text or interactive elements failing WCAG AA contrast in real time, so designers see problems instantly—not after a user complains. The trade-off is a small performance hit during rapid prototyping, but it prevents costly fixes later and keeps the interface consistently readable.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker risks training designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt alarms—if every change triggers a flag, they’ll learn to dismiss them. Instead, ship a pre-commit hook that blocks merges until contrast passes, forcing deliberate fixes rather than habituated clicks. Settle it by testing both: measure how often designers override live warnings versus how often they bypass the pre-commit block.
